metadata.title: Skyy Moore Has Limited Week 5 Appeal
metadata.description: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Skyy Moore caught one of two targets for minus-two yards against Tampa Bay after drawing seven targets against Atlanta the previous week. Moore has seen more playing time since Jayden Reed (neck) was lost for the season, but his Week 4 usage showed how difficult his volume can be to predict. Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, and Tucker Kraft remain ahead of him for targets in Green Bay's passing game. Savion Williams (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday, removing one potential threat to Moore's playing time for another week. Chicago also presents a difficult matchup, allowing only four passing touchdowns through four games while holding opponents below 200 passing yards per game. Moore will continue to have a role, but two targets last week are not enough to trust in fantasy lineups. RotoBaller ranks Moore WR86 for Week 5, making him a deep-league stash rather than a starting option.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - One catch in win
metadata.description: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-two yards while also adding 52 kickoff-return yards and 19 yards as a punt returner during Sunday's 17-14 win over the Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: Moore was unable to build off his seven targets from Week 3, garnering his fewest targets since Week 1 in the team's marginal victory versus Tampa Bay. The 26-year-old doesn't carry much upside as a fantasy asset, and he figures to operate as a distant No. 3 option at wide receiver behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden moving forward.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - Elevated to WR3 role with Reed done
metadata.description: Coach Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Moore will be the next man up at wide receiver after it was announced Jayden Reed (neck) will undergo season-ending surgery, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
metadata.analysis: With Reed out last Thursday night against the Falcons, Moore played 34 of 66 offensive snaps and ran 27 routes on Jordan Love's 55 dropbacks. Moore caught three of seven targets for 31 yards. He's expected to fight for scraps behind all three of Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the pecking order for targets.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore a Sneaky Waiver-Wire Pickup Amid Growing Role
metadata.description: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Skyy Moore has seen his involvement in the offense grow with each passing week through the first three weeks of the 2026 campaign. Moore played just four offensive snaps in the season-opening loss to the division-rival Minnesota Vikings and failed to catch his lone target. In the Week 2 overtime win over the New York Jets, the 26-year-old played 36% of the offensive snaps and caught two of three targets for six yards. Moore's role expanded even more in Thursday night's loss to the Atlanta Falcons, as he played 52% of the offensive snaps and caught three of his seven targets for 31 yards with fellow wideout Jayden Reed (neck) sidelined. The Packers are still unsure if Reed will even return at all in 2026, so Moore could become an interesting WR3 option for the Packers' passing game behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, especially with Green Bay's ground game going nowhere. The former second-rounder by the Kansas City Chiefs in 2022 from Western Michigan caught 43 passes for 494 yards in his first two years in KC, but it came with only one touchdown, and he quickly fell out of favor with the Chiefs. Right now, Moore is rostered in only 1% of Yahoo leagues.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - Sees seven targets in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Moore logged three catches on seven targets for 31 yards while adding 134 yards on five kickoff returns during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Moore has seen his playing time on offense steadily increase over the first three games of the regular season, and his 34 snaps on offense Thursday were third-most among wide receivers behind Matthew Golden (54) and Christian Watson (53). Not only were Moore's seven targets third-most among Green Bay wide receivers, they were also a career high for the 2022 second-rounder. The Packers' ground game has struggled due to injuries on the offensive line and the absence of Josh Jacobs (personal), which could mean a higher scoring floor for Moore and the rest of Green Bay's pass catchers.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore snags three passes in loss
metadata.description: Skyy Moore caught three of seven targets for 31 yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Moore found himself in a decent-sized role on the Packers' offense, though while seven targets sound nice, it was truly just a 13.7% target share, not counting throwaways. Still, with Jayden Reed out, he could be an interesting PPR option for those in deep leagues. Just don't spend too much FAAB or bust a waiver priority to get him.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore sees seven targets in loss
metadata.description: Skyy Moore caught three of seven targets for 31 yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Moore filled in admirably for the Jayden Reed role in this offense. While he's a bit of an unknown right now, he's still worth keeping an eye on and maybe even rostering as long as Reed is out.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore's Big Return Doesn't Make Him a Priority Add
metadata.description: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Skyy Moore finally made a splash in Week 2, but almost all of it came on special teams. Moore caught two passes for six yards against the Jets and ripped off a 63-yard punt return that helped set up the game-tying field goal. Jayden Reed (neck) is now dealing with an injury serious enough that head coach Matt LaFleur said it is too early to know whether he will play again this season. That opens snaps, but it does not automatically make Moore a fantasy starter. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden remain ahead of him in the passing game, and Moore has only two catches through two weeks. RotoBaller's September 23 mid-week waiver rankings have him 61st overall and recommend him only in 14-team PPR leagues. Moore is worth a deep-league stash while Reed's situation develops, but standard-league managers should wait for actual target volume before spending a roster spot.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - Sees more action in Week 2
metadata.description: Moore caught two of three targets for six yards during Sunday's 20-17 overtime win versus the Jets.
metadata.analysis: Moore logged just four snaps in the 39-22 loss to the Vikings in Week 1, though it was a different story in Week 2, with the wideout appearing in 21 of the Packers' 59 offensive snaps against the Jets, finishing behind Christian Watson (53) and Matthew Golden (51) after Jayden Reed (back) lasted just two offensive plays. However, despite the increased workload, Moore didn't do anything meaningful for fantasy managers. That's not expected to change anytime soon, even if Watson or Golden aren't available at some point moving ahead.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore catches two passes in Week 2
metadata.description: Skyy Moore caught two of his three targets for six yards in the Packers' 20-17 win over the New York Jets in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Moore has struggled to make an impact in the Green Bay passing attack to begin the season, recording three targets or less in each of the first two games. The wideout can remains off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 3 clash with the Atlanta Falcons.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - Logs 17 return yards versus Vikings
metadata.description: Moore failed to catch his only target and returned two punts for 17 yards during Green Bay's loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Moore saw the majority of his playing time on special teams, seeing 11 snaps compared to only four on offense. The 2022 second-round pick will likely continue to serve as the team's primary returner going forward while seeing limited action on offense.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - Set for prominent special-teams role
metadata.description: Moore will operate as the Packers' primary retuner on both kicks and punts to open the regular season, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Moore inked a one-year deal with Green Bay in March, and he'll step in as the team's go-to option on both kicks and punts. The wide receiver notched 907 kickoff-return yards and 291 yards as a punt returner over 17 regular-season contests with San Francisco last year. Moore has combined to catch five of 10 targets for 87 yards over the last two campaigns, so he doesn't carry much fantasy value in 2026.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore signs with Packers
metadata.description: The Packers agreed to terms with WR Skyy Moore on a one-year contract.
metadata.analysis: Moore held a role on special teams in the return game for the 49ers last season. He will likely hold a similar role for Green Bay.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - Expected to ink with Green Bay
metadata.description: Moore has agreed to terms on a one-year contract with the Packers, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports. Per Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, Moore's deal has a base value of $2.5 million with incentives to earn as much as $4.5 million.
metadata.analysis: Moore was productive while operating as a return man for the 49ers in 2025, totaling 907 kickoff-return yards and 291 yards fielding punts across 17 regular-season appearances. He also had five catches for 87 yards (seven targets) and two carries for 11 yards. Moore figures to primarily contribute in the return game again for his new team, as second-year wideout Savion Williams (foot) already projects within the Packers' plans for a gadget role on offense. Moore and Williams figure to also compete for opportunities returning kicks.

metadata.title: Packers Sign Skyy Moore to One-Year Deal
metadata.description: The Green Bay Packers signed former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver/returner Skyy Moore to an undisclosed one-year deal on Tuesday, sources told Jordan Schultz of FOX Sports. Moore averaged 27.5 yards per kick return and 11.6 yards per punt return last year with San Francisco. On offense, the 25-year-old former second-round pick (54th overall) by the Kansas City Chiefs in 2022 out of Western Michigan only caught five of seven targets for 87 yards in 17 regular-season games. Moore didn't do a ton in his first three years with the Chiefs on offense, either, contributing just 43 receptions on 74 targets for 494 yards and one touchdown in 36 games (11 starts). More than anything else, Moore will give the Packers a boost on special teams as a return man. In fantasy football, however, he should continue to be ignored across the board.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - Finds home in SF as return man
metadata.description: Moore finished the 2025 regular season with five receptions for 87 yards, two carries for 11 yards and 1,198 combined return yards in 17 appearances.
metadata.analysis: Moore was traded to the 49ers this past offseason after falling out of favor as a receiver during his three years with the Chiefs. The shifty wideout was used sparingly on offense (seven touches for 98 yards), but he solidified a role on special teams as San Francisco's primary return man. Moore appeared in all 17 games this regular season and finished with career highs in kick return yards (907) and punt return yards (291). The 24-year-old is a strong candidate to return to the 49ers next season after thriving as the team's return specialist in 2025.

metadata.title: Skyy Moore - Notches first down on rush
metadata.description: Moore carried once for 10 yards and brought back two punts for 11 yards and four kickoffs for 92 yards in Sunday's 42-38 win over the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Moore played just four of the 49ers' 72 snaps on offense in the win, but he made his mark during his time on the field. His 10-yard carry early in the second quarter was good for a first down, extending a drive that culminated in Brock Purdy's three-yard rushing touchdown. Moore also made a splash on special teams, with his 92 kickoff return yards marking his fourth-best total of the season. He'll continue to serve as the 49ers' top return man in Saturday's regular-season finale versus the Seahawks.
